commonPitfall.title: Common Pitfall
commonPitfall.body: Many textbooks first teach 全然 with negative expressions: 全然分からない means “I don’t understand at all.” In modern conversational Japanese, 全然 is also frequently used with positive expressions, such as 全然大丈夫, meaning “It’s totally fine.” Learners should recognize both patterns.

keywords.meaning: not at all; completely (casual positive usage)
keywords.nuance: Traditionally, 全然 is paired with negative expressions to mean 'not at all.' In modern conversational Japanese, especially among younger speakers, it is also commonly used before positive expressions such as 全然大丈夫 ('It's totally fine'). Learners should recognize both patterns.

questions.prompt: その映画は全然面白くなかった。
questions.answer: That movie wasn't interesting at all.

questions.hint: This is the modern positive usage of 全然.
questions.answer: It's totally fine. / No worries at all.

questions.prompt: 日本語は全然難しくないですよ。
